100	        start = self.rawdata[i:i+3]
101	        c = ord(start[-1])
102	        is_data = len(start) < 3 or not (65 <= c <= 90 or 97 <= c <= 122)
103	        pos = super().parse_endtag(i) if not is_data else -1
104	        if pos == -1:

122	class HTMLExtractor(htmlparser.HTMLParser):
123	    """
124	    Extract raw HTML from text.
125	
126	    The raw HTML is stored in the [`htmlStash`][markdown.util.HtmlStash] of the
127	    [`Markdown`][markdown.Markdown] instance passed to `md` and the remaining text
128	    is stored in `cleandoc` as a list of strings.

131	    def __init__(self, md: Markdown, *args, **kwargs):
132	        if 'convert_charrefs' not in kwargs:
133	            kwargs['convert_charrefs'] = False
134	
135	        # Block tags that should contain no content (self closing)
136	        self.empty_tags = set(['hr'])
137	
138	        self.lineno_start_cache = [0]
139	
140	        # This calls self.reset
141	        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
142	        self.md = md
143	
144	    def reset(self):
145	        """Reset this instance.  Loses all unprocessed data."""
146	        self.inraw = False
147	        self.intail = False
148	        self.stack: list[str] = []  # When `inraw==True`, stack contains a list of tags
149	        self._cache: list[str] = []
150	        self.cleandoc: list[str] = []
151	        self.lineno_start_cache = [0]
152	
153	        super().reset()
154	
155	    def close(self):
156	        """Handle any buffered data."""
157	        super().close()
158	        if len(self.rawdata):
159	            # Temp fix for https://bugs.python.org/issue41989
160	            # TODO: remove this when the bug is fixed in all supported Python versions.
161	            if self.convert_charrefs and not self.cdata_elem:  # pragma: no cover
162	                self.handle_data(htmlparser.unescape(self.rawdata))
163	            else:
164	                self.handle_data(self.rawdata)
165	        # Handle any unclosed tags.
166	        if len(self._cache):
167	            self.cleandoc.append(self.md.htmlStash.store(''.join(self._cache)))
168	            self._cache = []
169	
170	    @property
171	    def line_offset(self) -> int:
172	        """Returns char index in `self.rawdata` for the start of the current line. """
173	        for ii in range(len(self.lineno_start_cache)-1, self.lineno-1):
174	            last_line_start_pos = self.lineno_start_cache[ii]
175	            lf_pos = self.rawdata.find('\n', last_line_start_pos)
176	            if lf_pos == -1:
177	                # No more newlines found. Use end of raw data as start of line beyond end.
178	                lf_pos = len(self.rawdata)
179	            self.lineno_start_cache.append(lf_pos+1)
180	
181	        return self.lineno_start_cache[self.lineno-1]
182	
183	    def at_line_start(self) -> bool:
184	        """
185	        Returns True if current position is at start of line.
186	
187	        Allows for up to three blank spaces at start of line.
188	        """
189	        if self.offset == 0:
190	            return True
191	        if self.offset > 3:

194	        return self.rawdata[self.line_offset:self.line_offset + self.offset].strip() == ''

196	    def get_endtag_text(self, tag: str) -> str:
197	        """
198	        Returns the text of the end tag.
199	
200	        If it fails to extract the actual text from the raw data, it builds a closing tag with `tag`.
201	        """
202	        # Attempt to extract actual tag from raw source text
203	        start = self.line_offset + self.offset
204	        m = htmlparser.endendtag.search(self.rawdata, start)
205	        if m:

        # Treat `</>` as normal data as it is not a real tag.
        if self.rawdata[i:i + 3] == '</>':
            self.handle_data(self.rawdata[i:i + 3])
            return i + 3

        self.__starttag_text = None
        endpos = self.check_for_whole_start_tag(i)
        if endpos < 0:
            self.handle_data(self.rawdata[i:i + 1])
            return i + 1
        rawdata = self.rawdata
        self.__starttag_text = rawdata[i:endpos]

        # Now parse the data between `i+1` and `j` into a tag and `attrs`
        attrs = []
        match = htmlparser.tagfind_tolerant.match(rawdata, i+1)
        assert match, 'unexpected call to parse_starttag()'
        k = match.end()
        self.lasttag = tag = match.group(1).lower()
        while k < endpos:
            m = htmlparser.attrfind_tolerant.match(rawdata, k)
            if not m:
                break
            attrname, rest, attrvalue = m.group(1, 2, 3)
            if not rest:
                attrvalue = None
            elif attrvalue[:1] == '\'' == attrvalue[-1:] or \
                 attrvalue[:1] == '"' == attrvalue[-1:]:  # noqa: E127
                attrvalue = attrvalue[1:-1]
            if attrvalue:
                attrvalue = htmlparser.unescape(attrvalue)
            attrs.append((attrname.lower(), attrvalue))
            k = m.end()

        end = rawdata[k:endpos].strip()
        if end not in (">", "/>"):
            lineno, offset = self.getpos()
            if "\n" in self.__starttag_text:
                lineno = lineno + self.__starttag_text.count("\n")
                offset = len(self.__starttag_text) \
                         - self.__starttag_text.rfind("\n")  # noqa: E127
            else:
                offset = offset + len(self.__starttag_text)
            self.handle_data(rawdata[i:endpos])
            return endpos
        if end.endswith('/>'):
            # XHTML-style empty tag: `<span attr="value" />`
            self.handle_startendtag(tag, attrs)
        else:
            # *** set `cdata_mode` first so we can override it in `handle_starttag` (see #1036) ***
            if tag in self.CDATA_CONTENT_ELEMENTS:
                self.set_cdata_mode(tag)
            self.handle_starttag(tag, attrs)
        return endpos

content.text:
The bug is fixed: the `` example from the report now renders as a single `

…

` with the comment kept inside it. The full test suite passes. **Cause:** `` isn't a block-level tag, so the HTML extractor (`markdown/htmlparser.py`) passes it through as inline text and doesn't track it as an open tag. When a comment comes at the start of a line, `handle_empty_tag` always stores it as its own raw HTML block, with blank lines around it. That broke the paragraph in two, leaving `` in one `

` and `` in the next. **Fix:** - **`markdown/htmlparser.py`:** the extractor now keeps a list of inline tags that are still open in the current paragraph. Self-closing tags like `` and `` are ignored because they never get a closing tag. The list is cleared at a blank line or when a block-level raw HTML block starts. A line-start comment (or other declaration or processing instruction) only becomes its own block when no inline tag is open; otherwise it stays inline. The tracking lives in three small helper methods. - **`markdown/extensions/md_in_html.py`:** this extension handles inline tags itself instead of going through the base methods, so it had the same bug. It now calls the same helpers, including inside `markdown="1"` blocks, and clears the list when such a block opens or closes. **Unchanged:** a comment on its own line after plain paragraph text, or after inline HTML that has already been closed, still splits the paragraph as before (`foo\n\nbar` gives `

foo

\n\n

bar

`). **Tests:** I added three tests to `tests/test_syntax/blocks/test_html_blocks.py`: the reported case, a comment after a closed inline tag, and a comment after a blank line ends the paragraph. These also run with `md_in_html` enabled through the existing subclass. I added one nested `markdown="1"` test to `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_md_in_html.py`. **Results:** before the change: 1030 passed, 110 skipped. After: 1040 passed, 110 skipped, with no regressions. Two test files fail to collect in both runs because PyYAML isn't installed. **Two things to know:** - **Test setup:** the venv doesn't have the package's registration info, so extension short names like `md_in_html` don't resolve and most extension tests fail with a plain `pytest` run. For the comparison I put a temporary file with that info in a temp folder outside the repo. Nothing was installed and nothing was added to the repo. - **Line endings:** one of my early scripted edits turned the LF line endings in `htmlparser.py` into CRLF. I restored the file from the committed version before making the final edits, and `git diff` now shows only the intended changes.
